judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration/reliance preamble with no operative term capable of two readings; nothing vague to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It simply incorporates the declarations and 'all the terms of this policy', consistent with Condition 12 (Declarations, c035); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed, capped list of supplementary payments ($250 bail bond, $25 per day) with little interpretive play, though 'all expenses incurred by the company' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly modified by the HPL First Aid Exclusion (c049), the Incidental Medical Malpractice provision (c158) and the prejudgment interest endorsement (c169), so its content must be read across several instruments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare definitional preamble; no term to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It confirms endorsements are covered by the definitions, which is what the many amendatory endorsements assume; no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Circular but conventional definition keyed to 'mobile equipment', a defined term; boundary questions are possible but not acute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with the mobile-equipment definition (c012) and the auto exclusions; no contradiction located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Bodily injury ... which occurs during the policy period' is the classic trigger phrase courts construe for latent or continuing injury.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Broad Form endorsement (c158) amends this definition to include Incidental Medical Malpractice Injury while the HPL part uses 'injury' caused by a 'medical incident' (c038, c046), leaving two different injury concepts in one instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition ends with liability assumed under an 'incident contract' where the defined term is 'incidental contract' (c010) — a mechanical slip that changes the reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy uses 'incident contract'; the mistake is intrinsic rather than a clash with another clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long enumerated definition with the phrase 'operations of reliance upon a representation' (for 'or'), plus a three-limb completion test that could be applied differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the products hazard (c017) and the aggregate limit subparagraphs (c132, c166); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed inclusion/exclusion list ('but does not include ... a dumbwaiter ... not exceeding four feet') that is specific rather than vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Ties into the elevator exclusion (c125) and incidental contract (c010) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise carve-outs, though the transcription 'independent [contractors]' is garbled and it again refers to an 'incidental contract'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Harmonises with exclusion (q) (c130), which keys the explosion hazard to classification symbols; no clash located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of five contract types with no catch-all, inviting expressio unius arguments about contracts not listed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Broad Form endorsement I.(A) extends the same defined term to 'any oral or written contract or agreement relating to the conduct of the named insured's business', so the policy carries two very different versions of 'incidental contract'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Severability language ('applies separately to each insured ... except with respect to the limits') is short and general but its meaning is settled by convention.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It points to the 'Persons Insured' provisions, which have been rewritten several times (c051-c062, c161, c183), so who is an 'insured' must be traced through competing endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An exhaustive four-limb definition with concrete examples; little room for two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 'automobile' (c004) and the mobile equipment exclusions and Persons Insured (e) (c131).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line pointer to Item 1 of the declarations; nothing ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-052 (c092) and Endorsement 13 (c211) make a dozen other entities 'named insureds' though only one entity appears in Item 1, so the defined term does not match the instrument as endorsed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing vending-machine/rented-property carve-out is awkwardly worded but the definition is otherwise concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with the products hazard definition (c017) as redefined by Form 009-136 (c195); no direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Accident ... neither expected nor intended from the standpoint of the insured' is among the most frequently construed phrases in liability policies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Broad Form Extended Bodily Injury provision (c162) expands 'occurrence' to certain intentional acts, and the HPL part uses 'medical incident' (c046) rather than occurrence, so the trigger concepts sit uneasily together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-limb geographic definition; each limb is specific, though limb (2)'s travel proviso is convoluted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is amended by Limited Worldwide Liability (c160) and displaced for HPL by the policy-territory endorsements (c045, c172, c205), leaving several territory rules to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'away from premises owned by or rented to the named insured' proviso is a familiar but workable boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-136 (c195) redefines 'products hazard' and drops the away-from-premises requirement, so two definitions of the same term appear in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Physical injury to or destruction of tangible property' plus loss-of-use is a standard formulation, occasionally litigated but not internally unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Nuclear Energy endorsement (c201) expands 'property damage' to include radioactive contamination, an expressly stated variation rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerated property types with a 'and similar property' tail, but the operative trigger (mechanical equipment for listed excavation work) is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches exclusion (q)(3) (c130) keyed to the 'u' symbol; no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanical premium-computation language; 'advance premium is a deposit premium only' is clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to an 'audit period designated in the declarations', but the declarations designate none, and the Pay Plan endorsement (c113) sets a different payment regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive inspection right with an express disclaimer; the drafting is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the premium record-keeping duty in Condition 1 (c020); nothing to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional on certification under a motor-vehicle financial responsibility law; the trigger and reimbursement duty are stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Vehicle risks are excluded from HPL (c042 as amended by c188) and CGL (c123), so this condition sits oddly in a hospital policy but does not contradict a specific clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As soon as practicable' notice of an 'occurrence' is a stock but genuinely elastic standard that courts do construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is superseded for HPL by Condition VI (c048) and again by the Wisconsin endorsement (c095), which substitutes 'as soon as reasonably possible' and a claim-based rather than occurrence-based trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Immediately forward ... every demand, notice, summons or other process' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated nearly verbatim in the HPL amended condition (c048), so the duplication is consistent rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Cooperation duty with a voluntary-payment bar; broad but conventional and rarely internally unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The HPL amended condition (c048) restates it with wider reach (each employee, officers, stockholders) and drops the first-aid carve-out that Supplementary Payments (c002) preserves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A no-action clause with a condition precedent of 'full compliance with all of the terms of this policy'; the phrase is broad but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement (c114) deletes this condition 'in its entirety' and replaces it, while the Professional Liability Amendatory Endorsement states flatly that 'the Action Against Company Condition does not apply' (c098) — three inconsistent positions on the same condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Primary insurance, except when stated to apply in excess of or contingent upon' is clear in structure though the excess/contingent trigger requires cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fire Legal Liability (c155), Broad Form Property Damage (c157), the medical staff extension (c186) and Non-Owned Watercraft (c159) each make coverage excess or non-contributory, so the primacy rule is qualified in several places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical contribution formula; arithmetic rather than interpretation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Operates only through the introductory Other Insurance clause (c027) and does not clash with the excess provisions it is subordinate to.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A proportionate-limits formula stated in one sentence with no elastic term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paired with (a) (c028) under c027; no other clause contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional subrogation and cooperation clause; nothing vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin endorsement (c115) adds a made-whole limitation, so the unqualified 'subrogated to all the insured's rights' must be read down.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Anti-waiver language; the operative rule (change only by endorsement) is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both Wisconsin endorsements (c096 and c116) reverse the first sentence by making an agent's knowledge the company's knowledge, directly contradicting 'notice to any agent ... shall not effect a waiver'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assignment consent plus a death-of-named-insured rule; concrete, if odd for a corporate insured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The named insured is a corporation (declarations Item 1), so the death provision is inert but does not contradict any clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional rule expressed clearly ('if this policy is issued for a period of three years').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declared policy period is one year (03/01/1996-03/01/1997), so the condition never engages; that is surplusage rather than contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cancellation mechanics and thirty-day notice are stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 4 requires sixty days' notice (c069), the Wisconsin cancellation form allows ten days for non-payment and mid-term cancellation (c108, c109) and the Professional Liability Amendatory adds further grounds (c099) — several inconsistent notice periods for the same act.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An integration/representation clause; 'embodies all agreements existing' is broad but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both Wisconsin endorsements (c097, c117) add a paragraph materially limiting the misrepresentation consequences this clause assumes, and the policy is in fact made up of many separate endorsement documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attaching language with no operative content beyond the effective date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 1 bears the policy inception date, so 'effective on the inception date unless otherwise stated' causes no dissonance here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unlicensed physicians' is undefined and the conditional grant ('if the institutions ... do not follow them with their respective coverages ... but not otherwise') plus the typo 'this coverage with apply' leave the scope genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deems non-employees to be treated as employees, which must be squared with the Persons Insured form that excludes licensed physicians (c056) and with the medical staff extension (c183, c185) limiting physicians to administrative acts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant turns on 'injury ... caused by a medical incident which occurs during the policy period', and 'injury' is not separately defined in this part while 'medical incident' is a defined aggregation concept.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the aggregation sentence in the medical incident definition (c046), the limits (c044) and the Broad Form Incidental Medical Malpractice coverage (c158), which grants malpractice-type cover under the CGL part.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard employee bodily-injury exclusion; 'arising out of and in the course of' employment is familiar and workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendatory Endorsement GL 00 32 (c170) deletes and replaces 'the exclusion relating to bodily injury to any employee of the insured' without saying which coverage part, so it is unclear whether HPL exclusion (a) survives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Statutory-benefit exclusion with the tail 'or under similar law', a modest general-after-specific tail.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors the CGL workers' compensation exclusion; no clause contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excluding 'liability of an insured, if an individual, for such insured's personal acts or omissions involving a medical incident' is a striking carve-out that could be read to gut individual coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Persons Insured endorsement declares exclusion (c) 'not applicable' (c060) and the medical staff extension disapplies it for medical staff (c184), so its residual field of operation is genuinely uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional vehicle/watercraft/aircraft exclusion, plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-050 (c188) rewrites it with a professional-services exception and Endorsement No. 5 (c071) amends that form again for air ambulances, so three versions of exclusion (d) must be layered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short three-limb list of insureds tied to the declarations designation; definite in itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin form 009-109 (c051-c059) states that the persons insured provisions 'are changed to read as follows', wholly displacing this list, yet the original remains printed in the coverage part.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'each medical incident' cap depends on an aggregation rule and the schedule figures are garbled, making the per-incident/aggregate boundary the natural site of dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declarations state $400,000/$4,000,000 while the coverage part schedule states 400/1,000 thousand, the PCF endorsement raises limits to $1,000,000/$3,000,000 (c173) and Form 041 applies limits separately by location/entity (c193).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause reads 'anywhere in the [world] ... provided the original suit ... is brought within the United States', a broad grant with a proviso whose reach depends on the missing text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Two successive Wisconsin endorsements amend this very provision (c172, c205) and Endorsement No. 10 deletes the first of them (c203), leaving competing territory language on the page.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any act or omission in the furnishing of professional health care services' plus 'all related acts or omissions ... to any one person shall be considered one medical incident' is precisely the sort of aggregation language parties read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives the per-incident limit (c044), sits alongside the separate 'occurrence' definition (c015) and overlaps the CGL Incidental Medical Malpractice grant (c158), so the same conduct can be characterised under two regimes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow inclusive definition; 'required to submit or has submitted with the company's consent' is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Broad Form arbitration condition (c137) and the duty to defend 'any suit' (c038); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notice 'as soon as practicable' of any claim or of 'specific circumstances involving a particular person likely to result in a claim' is an elastic reporting trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes Condition 4 (c023-c025) but the Wisconsin professional liability endorsement (c095) replaces subparagraph 4(a) again with a different standard, so the operative notice duty must be assembled from three texts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence exclusion whose effect on Supplementary Payments is expressly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes what Supplementary Payments (c002)(c) grants and what the cooperation clause (c025) preserves, and the Incidental Medical Malpractice provision (c158) excludes first aid again — consistent in direction but spread across clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as stated in this Part, this policy does not apply to injury caused by any medical incident' is a sweeping, one-sentence carve-out whose reach across the whole policy is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Broad Form endorsement expressly grants Incidental Medical Malpractice Liability Coverage under the CGL part (c158) and the charitable-care endorsements extend 'the coverages provided by this policy' to community health care (c090, c196), all of which this sentence would negate.
